parameters.cooling_method: cooled in equipment to room temperature

evidence.quote: The specimens were heated at a speed of 100 /C176C/min in the SPS equipment until reaching the final sintering temperature (800, 1000 and 1200 /C176C), kept at the final sintering temperature for 10 min and then cooled in the equipment to room temperature. Throughout the sintering process, the applied axial pressure was always 50 MPa.

evidence.quote: The specimens were heated at a speed of 100 /C176C/min in the SPS equipment until reaching the final sintering temperature (800, 1000 and 1200 /C176C), kept at the final sintering temperature for 10 min and then cooled in the equipment to room temperature. Throughout the sintering process, the applied axial pressure was always 50 MPa.
The alloys mainly consist of a phase when the sintering temperature is below the b transus temperature of Ti.
The a phase, a'' phase, b phase and a-Zr phase show diffraction peaks in the alloys sintered at 800 /C176C.
When the sintering temperature is 1000 /C176C, strong diffraction peaks of b phase and weak diffraction peaks of a'' phase in the alloys, indicating that Nb, Zr and Fe have been well diffused in Ti.
Since the mole fraction of Zr is up to 25% in alloys, some peaks corresponding to a-Zr phase can be found in the XRD patterns.
Due to the local segregation of Fe, the diffraction peaks corresponding to intermetallic compounds Fe2Zr and FeTi appear in Ti-15Nb-25Zr-8Fe-1000.
Due to the local segregation of Fe, the diffraction peaks corresponding to intermetallic compounds Fe2Zr and FeTi appear in Ti-15Nb-25Zr-8Fe-1000.
When the temperature is 1200 /C176C (Fig. 4c), more b grains are observed with segregation of Nb still existing.
When the temperature is increased to 1000 /C176C, grain boundaries appear and become more obvious with addition of Fe.
Ti, Nb, Zr, and Fe are not uniformly distributed and the segregations of Nb, Zr and Fe are found in Ti-15Nb-25Zr-4Fe-800 (Fig. 1).
No sig\ufb01cant pores are observed in the microstructures of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-(0, 4, 8)Fe (Fig. 4) indicating that the raw powders are well combined with each other.

Ti-15Nb-25Zr-(4, 8)Fe-800 show similar stress plateau and the fracture strains are 18 and 15%, respectively, which are larger than that of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-800.
As the sintering temperature is increased, the compressive strength of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-4Fe shows an increasing trend and the plasticity is almost not changed.
The r0.2 and rb of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-4Fe-1000 are higher than those of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-1000 owing to the solid-solution strengthening effect of Fe.

Similar as the micro-Vickers hardness, the r0.2 and rb of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-8Fe-1000 are a little lower than those of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-4Fe-1000, because the appearance of intermetallic compounds in Ti-15Nb-25Zr-8Fe-1000 leads to insufficient diffusion of the alloying elements (Ref 32).

The r0.2 and rb of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-4Fe-1000 are higher than those of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-1000 owing to the solid-solution strengthening effect of Fe.
It is supposed that grain boundaries become weak after high temperature sintering, thus the plasticity of Ti-15Nb-25Zr-8Fe-1200 is significantly reduced.
